repositories.value: Reverse engineering of shipped binaries, packages and runtime behavior.
repositories.assessment: A legitimate Claude Code/Codex plugin: both native manifests and a public workflow skill are present. Keep it as an optional tool integration for explicitly requested artifact/runtime analysis, not a dependency of ordinary source-code architecture work. Reuse its distinction between direct evidence, inference and unknowns.
repositories.requirements: Node MCP runtime; native analysis may require Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna and additional platform support. The skill itself explicitly says loading it does not install/register the runtime.

repositories.value: Domain language, module boundaries, prototypes and handoffs.
repositories.assessment: Keep the selected methods already integrated. Its current tree contains additional material, but a larger catalog is not a reason to restore setup interviews or another general router.
repositories.requirements: Markdown methods; some upstream workflows assume setup scripts and host-specific commands.

repositories.value: Planning, debugging, tests and development workflow.
repositories.assessment: Keep the coordinated workflow backbone. Do not reintroduce mandatory discovery/planning/review cycles on every small task or unconditional delegation.
repositories.requirements: Instruction methods are portable; upstream hooks and exact host tools are separate capabilities.

repositories.value: Agent configuration security scanning; a large engineering and learning catalog.
repositories.assessment: Adapt the threat checklist for skill/plugin intake: instruction files, permissions, hooks, MCP definitions, secrets and install-time commands. Its security-scan delegates to AgentShield; that scanner is an additional dependency, not a capability supplied by Markdown. Do not import automatic instinct learning.
repositories.requirements: AgentShield is a separate npm tool. Continuous-learning-v2 requires observation hooks, background analysis and persistent storage.

repositories.value: Assumptions, small changes, simplicity and verifiable goals.
repositories.assessment: No second coding philosophy. These principles already inform the shared policy. The original forrestchang URL resolves to this repository; count it once. This is community work inspired by Karpathy, not a Karpathy-authored package.
repositories.requirements: Instruction-only core. No root LICENSE was present in the inspected tree; do not copy text until notice requirements are resolved.

repositories.value: Application web-data integration: search, scraping, extraction and browser interaction.
repositories.assessment: Useful when a project actually selects Firecrawl. Do not import its broad activation rule that steers any app-level web-data request to Firecrawl or make an API provider mandatory. Existing sources/api/security workflows already supply the general method.
repositories.license_assessment: AGPL-3.0 host; sampled build skill declares ISC
repositories.requirements: FIRECRAWL_API_KEY and SDK/cloud or configured self-hosted service. Apply exact file-specific terms; do not relabel the entire upstream repository MIT.

repositories.value: Skill authoring/evaluation, design and document tooling.
repositories.assessment: Use the evaluation methodology to strengthen the existing skill-authoring workflow: baseline versus skill, positive/negative triggering cases, repeated samples and observable outcomes. Frontend-design is another useful design reference. Document editing is an optional separate domain, not core engineering scope.
repositories.license_assessment: Per skill; sampled frontend-design and docx Apache-2.0
repositories.requirements: Skill-creator includes Python evaluation scripts and assumes an agent execution harness. Document skills have their own runtimes. Reading instructions does not install these dependencies.

repositories.value: Small complete solutions plus audit/debt/gain reports.
repositories.assessment: Retain the established common philosophy and the three preserved report skills. Existing Ponytail benchmark figures are not Unified Engineering performance results.
repositories.requirements: Instruction-based behavior works in the existing plugin. Upstream lifecycle scripts remain separate, unverified managed-host functionality.

repositories.value: Prompt/skill discovery and retrieval through a real Claude plugin.
repositories.assessment: Can help discover skills, but a registry result is untrusted input requiring source/license/script review. Existing plugin discovery already serves much of this purpose. No second global router or automatic registry-skill installation.
repositories.license_assessment: Root split MIT/CC0; sampled plugin/skill declares MIT
repositories.requirements: Configured prompts.chat MCP service. Registry search does not establish installed skill discovery, security or managed-host compatibility.

repositories.value: Concrete typography, palettes, layout, design-system and stack references.
repositories.assessment: Add a focused visual-design reference under frontend. Preserve the project house style, accessibility and content needs; do not impose a catalog-selected style on every UI or copy the full corpus into context.
repositories.license_assessment: MIT root; font/assets have separate metadata
repositories.requirements: Its local search uses Python 3 and standard-library data files; an installation CLI is separate. Review exact selected files and asset notices before importing.

repositories.value: Structured specifications, process templates and generated agent skills.
repositories.assessment: Borrow explicit requirement-to-check traceability when a project needs it. The generator source actually registers/renders SKILL.md artifacts. Do not install another project operating system or repeat the existing design/plan/implement workflow for small tasks.
repositories.requirements: Specify CLI, installed process/preset templates and project-generated artifacts. A skill generator is labeled separately from a ready-made instruction pack.

repositories.value: Persistent source/document knowledge graphs with traceable edges and query/explain tools.
repositories.assessment: Useful on a large repository with repeated navigation needs. Prefer focused tracing first. Its broad any-codebase-question trigger and full scan should not become default policy. The public Codex adapter is real; lowercase skill.md is not evidence of invalidity or insecurity.
repositories.requirements: Python CLI/package, parsing/rendering dependencies and generated graph artifacts. Semantic/enrichment paths must distinguish inferred edges from deterministic source links.

repositories.value: An examples repository that also distributes public installable skills.
repositories.assessment: Do not count it as a link-only awesome list: its agent_skills directory contains executable instructions. Commit archaeology and dependency reasoning may inform context/debug references. Reject automatic multi-model fan-out as default behavior; the sampled orchestrator calls external CLIs/APIs and includes bypass-permission flags.
repositories.requirements: Varies by skill. Sampled orchestration requires shell/jq and external model CLIs or API keys. None were invoked. Model orchestration is not supplied by copying the prose.

repositories.value: A public agent skill driving end-to-end video creation.
repositories.assessment: Useful as a separate video-production capability, not an engineering-quality workflow. Do not adopt automatic install/config actions, fixed Chinese portrait defaults or provider choices in a general coding plugin.
repositories.requirements: Sampled skill supports macOS/Windows, uses uv and its adjacent Python helper, and needs configured model/media providers and rendering dependencies. Managed Linux/Android compatibility not established.

repositories.value: Browser QA, release and evidence-oriented engineering roles.
repositories.assessment: Borrow scoped QA charters and reproducible evidence, which extend existing browser/test/ship skills. The complete generated workflows are too operationally coupled and repetitive for this plugin.
repositories.requirements: Bun/Git and built browser/runtime helpers; transcripts, telemetry/config and host-specific commands appear in workflows. Sampled review requires Agent dispatches. No blanket import.

repositories.value: Agent worktrees, terminals, browser and orchestration exposed through public skills.
repositories.assessment: Useful for someone who chooses the Orca environment. Keep its runtime-specific management outside the core; current native worktree and delegation workflows should use actual host tools. Do not replace the user Android ChatGPT workflow to obtain it.
repositories.requirements: Orca executable and its version-matched guide/runtime. The public orca-cli skill is a discovery stub, not an independent implementation.

repositories.value: Browser access for agents through public skills, CLI and supported browser connections.
repositories.assessment: Useful when no suitable browser tool is available and this integration is explicitly chosen. Existing browser/frontend/testing methods already cover the general checks. Do not impose its CLI over a supported native browser or reuse unrelated logged-in sessions.
repositories.requirements: browser-use CLI/Python package and a browser/CDP connection; hosted paths add cloud service configuration. No new browser runtime or package was installed.

repositories.value: Concise output and a larger compression/proxy ecosystem.
repositories.assessment: Keep answer-first, clear writing. Do not adopt a caveman persona, persistent extra voice mode or token/cost savings claims. Lite already reduces ceremony without dropping technical substance.
repositories.license_assessment: Apache-2.0 current root; components/history need notice review
repositories.requirements: The voice skill is text; automatic modes, compression, proxy and statistics are separate runtime capabilities.

repositories.value: Engineering specialists and workflow refinements.
repositories.assessment: Continue using the integrated specialists rather than loading a second duplicate collection. Only consider an upstream delta when it fixes a demonstrated gap.
repositories.requirements: Many methods portable; scripts, named tools, browser runners and stack-specific examples require capability checks.

repositories.value: Persistent observations and retrieval across sessions.
repositories.assessment: Useful only as an explicitly configured external memory integration. Prefer existing scoped handoffs in the core. Do not promise capture or future-session recall from a skill alone.
repositories.requirements: Node/Bun worker, SQLite and optional vector-search tooling; capture hooks/adapters and durable storage. README states anonymous analytics are enabled by default and cloud sync is opt-in.

repositories.value: Art direction, real content/assets and browser-backed design critique.
repositories.assessment: Reuse content-specific design critique under frontend. Do not adopt rigid one-section-per-screen, mandatory effects, startup gates or automatic image acquisition as universal policy.
repositories.requirements: Current SKILL.md embeds a Stop hook and references Node gate scripts and browser evidence. Text adaptation must not claim these gates ran.

repositories.value: Native Claude/Codex plugins for durable task delegation and team results.
repositories.assessment: Good ideas: stable task IDs, idempotent request IDs, inspect uncertain outcomes before retry, and distinguish submitted/running/complete. General API/observability/delegation methods overlap; the persistent autonomous-team platform is not appropriate as a core dependency.
repositories.requirements: Connected Paperclip person/company, configured agents and service execution capacity/budget. Its plugin creates real external work; requires an actual delegation request.

repositories.value: Read-only access to social/web content when existing tools cannot retrieve it.
repositories.assessment: Useful fallback for a concrete missing source, not a reason to install channels or request login every time a site is named. Existing public fetch/search/connected apps stay first. Preserve distinctions between a page shell, full text, comments and transcripts.
repositories.requirements: agent-reach CLI plus channel-specific backends, sessions or dependencies. The sampled skill explicitly prefers built-in tools and does not authorize installation merely from a URL mention.

repositories.value: Design critique, hierarchy, typography, polish and resilient UI states.
repositories.assessment: Best source for a concise, task-relevant visual critique procedure. Integrate with frontend and browser; avoid another router, 24 new top-level commands or automatic design/config files.
repositories.requirements: Text references are portable. Current workflow also uses helper scripts, optional live mode and design hooks; these are not automatically available in managed ChatGPT.

repositories.value: A native Claude plugin exposing a design app with skills and design systems.
repositories.assessment: Real companion plugin, not merely internal development skills. Useful if the user chooses that design platform; do not bundle its daemon, 139-skill surface or many design systems into this engineering core. Use a few portable visual-critique principles instead.
repositories.requirements: Sampled plugin explicitly requires the od daemon on PATH and stdio MCP. A large application/catalog is separate from instruction-only frontend guidance.

scope: Repositories shipping public user-facing Claude Code/Codex-compatible skills, generated skill workflows, or native plugins, including companion integrations for a larger product. Excludes link-only indexes, internal-only development skills, bare agent-persona lists, and host agent/model runtimes themselves. Stars belong to the entire repository, not an individual skill/plugin.

method.selection: Highest-starred eligible repositories found in the documented search; publicly exposed skill/plugin/generator source inspected. Not an exhaustive official GitHub category.
method.compatibility: Source inspection only. No new installs, hooks, external services or Android runtime tests.
